_metadata.description: Verified veterans treatment court data by state. Top 10 states by veteran population. Claude references this instead of generating VTC data from memory.
_metadata.anti_hallucination: If a county or eligibility detail is not in this file, the calculator MUST say: 'Veterans treatment court availability and eligibility vary by county. Contact your local court or VA Veterans Justice Outreach specialist for current program details.'

CA.statute: Cal. Penal Code 1170.9 (post-conviction sentencing); Cal. Penal Code 1001.80 (pretrial military diversion, expanded by SB 1025 eff. Jan 1, 2025)
CA.statewide_note: PC 1170.9 applies statewide as a sentencing provision any court must consider. Dedicated VTC courtrooms are optional per county.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: eligible -- may need VA waiver for benefits but court eligibility not barred
discharge_types.bad_conduct: eligible -- same VA waiver process as OTH
discharge_types.dishonorable: generally ineligible -- very difficult to receive VA waiver but can apply

eligibility.service_connection_detail: Must allege suffering from PTSD, TBI, MST, substance abuse, or other mental health condition as a result of military service. For PC 1001.80, condition must have been a significant factor in the offense.
charge_exclusions: Offenses requiring PC 290 sex offender registration (except PC 314 indecent exposure)
PC 220 -- Assault with intent to commit specified sex offenses
PC 264.1 -- Rape or sexual penetration in concert
PC 288.5 -- Continuous sexual abuse of a child
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: Exclusions above apply to PC 1001.80 pretrial diversion. PC 1170.9 post-conviction sentencing has fewer categorical exclusions.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Prior convictions do not automatically disqualify under PC 1170.9. Military diversion under PC 1001.80 is generally available only once.

program_details.completion_result_pretrial: All criminal charges dismissed; arrest deemed never to have occurred
program_details.completion_result_postconviction: Early termination of probation, felony reduction to misdemeanor (PC 17), dismissal under PC 1203.4 (expungement)

TX.statute: Tex. Gov't Code Ch. 124 (124.001-124.007); Tex. Gov't Code 411.0727 (nondisclosure after completion)
TX.statewide_note: Optional per county. Approximately 39 counties have programs. Counties may jointly establish regional programs (124.004).
TX.counties_note: 29 of approximately 39 counties verified. North Texas Regional Court serves Collin, Cooke, Fannin, Grayson, Hunt, Kaufman, Rockwall.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: varies by county -- Bexar accepts all; Dallas excludes
discharge_types.bad_conduct: varies by county -- Bexar accepts; most others exclude
discharge_types.dishonorable: varies by county -- Bexar accepts all discharge types; Dallas and most others exclude

eligibility.discharge_note: State statute does NOT specify discharge requirements. Each county sets its own policy.
eligibility.service_connection_detail: 124.002(a): must suffer from brain injury, mental illness, or mental disorder (including PTSD) or be a victim of MST, AND condition must have occurred during/resulted from military service AND affected the criminal conduct.
charge_exclusions: Injury to a child, elderly, or disabled person
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: Statute allows any misdemeanor or felony. Above exclusions are common across counties, aligned with Art. 42A.054(a).
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Varies by county. Dallas: no prior felony convictions. Fort Bend: no prior sex/drug delivery/3g convictions. Statute considers criminal history but imposes no categorical bar.

tracks.pretrial_diversion: Charges dismissed upon completion; potential expunction (124.001(b))
tracks.deferred_adjudication: Nondisclosure order eligible 2 years after completion (411.0727)

FL.statute: F.S. 394.47891 (Veterans Treatment Court Programs); F.S. 948.08(7) (felony pretrial veteran intervention); F.S. 948.16(2) (misdemeanor pretrial veteran intervention)
FL.statewide_note: Optional per circuit. Legislature encourages a VTC in each judicial circuit. 34 veterans courts statewide as of FY 2024-25.
FL.legislative_update: HB 199 (effective July 1, 2026): shifts admission from state attorney sole authority to court with multidisciplinary team; creates post-adjudicatory VTC track for nonviolent felonies.
FL.counties_note: 17 circuits verified. 34 total VTC programs across approximately 20 circuits.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: varies by circuit -- statute silent; circuits decide
discharge_types.bad_conduct: varies by circuit -- generally excluded where specified
discharge_types.dishonorable: generally ineligible -- chief judge and state attorney have exclusive authority to allow per 394.47891(3)(d)

eligibility.service_connection_detail: 394.47891(8)(a)(1): must have service-related mental health condition, TBI, substance use disorder, psychological problem, or military sexual trauma.
charge_exclusions: Lewd or lascivious offenses involving minors
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: Per F.S. 948.06(8)(c). Additional circuit-level exclusions common (felony DUI, drug distribution).
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: No categorical statutory bar. State attorney considers criminal history and prior VTC participation.

tracks.pretrial_diversion: Charges dismissed (nolle prosequi); expungement eligible under F.S. 943.0585
tracks.post_adjudicatory: NEW effective July 1, 2026 (HB 199) -- sentencing courts may divert for nonviolent felonies

conditions: Substance abuse and mental health treatment

PA.statewide_note: Optional per county. 26 county VTC programs as of 2025, covering 31 of 67 counties. First VTC: Lackawanna County, November 2009. Courts may accept defendants from other counties (916(d)).
PA.counties_note: 12 counties verified. DMVA reports 26 county programs. Regional courts expanding coverage.
PA.data_gaps: PA publishes limited eligibility details at the state level. Each county sets its own criteria via local rules.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: varies by county -- no statewide standard
discharge_types.dishonorable: varies by county -- no statewide standard

eligibility.discharge_note: 42 Pa.C.S. 916 does not specify discharge requirements.
eligibility.service_connection_detail: Programs target veterans struggling with addiction, mental illness, or co-occurring disorders, often caused by PTSD. Specifics vary by county.
charge_exclusions: Varies by county -- no statewide statutory exclusions in 916
Generally nonviolent offenders per problem-solving court model
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Not addressed at state level. Each county determines per local rules.

program_details.typical_duration: 12-24 months (Chester County: 1-2 years pretrial, 2-3 years post-conviction)

NY.statute: Judiciary Law 212(bb); CPL 170.15(5), 180.20(4), 230.11, 230.21 (case removal); CPL 390.30 (sentencing deferral)
NY.statewide_note: Optional per county. 38 VTCs in 29 of 62 counties. Adjoining-county transfers allowed.
NY.counties_note: 29 counties hosting 38 VTCs. Some counties have multiple courts.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: eligible -- NY accepts all discharge statuses
discharge_types.bad_conduct: eligible -- all characters of discharge accepted
discharge_types.dishonorable: eligible -- nycourts.gov states all discharge statuses accepted

eligibility.discharge_note: NY is notably inclusive. Restoration of Honor Act (2019) can restore state benefits for OTH+ discharges.
eligibility.service_connection_detail: Nexus between military service and criminal behavior expected. Clinical determination by treatment team.
charge_exclusions: Class A violent felonies (murder, arson, kidnapping)
Family offenses (CPL 530.11) -- cannot transfer to VTC in adjoining county
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: No statewide eligibility statute. Individual VTCs have discretion. DUI is 44.2% of all cases.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Not statutorily defined. Treatment team evaluates case-by-case.

program_details.completion_result: Charges reduced or dismissed; withdrawal of guilty plea possible; non-criminal disposition

OH.statute: No dedicated VTC statute. Authority: Ohio Supreme Court Rules of Superintendence Sup.R. 36.20-36.29. Related: ORC 2951.041 (Intervention in Lieu of Conviction)
OH.statewide_note: Optional per county. 28-29 certified VTCs as of late 2025. Certification renewed every 3 years.
OH.counties_note: 20 counties verified (~24 dockets). Chief Justice confirmed 28 certified VTCs.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: varies -- Cuyahoga accepts all; Greene/Montgomery require honorable/general
discharge_types.dishonorable: varies -- Cuyahoga accepts all; most others exclude

eligibility.service_connection_detail: Most courts require condition to be a significant factor in the offense. Combat experience NOT required.
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: Varies by county. ILC track (ORC 2951.041): F1-F3, violence, felony sex offenses, drug trafficking excluded.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: ILC track: no prior felony offense of violence. County VTCs: violent felonies generally disqualify; non-violent evaluated case-by-case.

tracks.diversion_ILC: Charges dismissed under ORC 2951.041. Record sealing eligible immediately.
tracks.non_diversion: Post-conviction. Completion may result in early termination.

conditions: Substance abuse and mental health treatment

NC.statute: N.C. Gen. Stat. Ch. 7A, Art. 62 (7A-790 through 7A-801) -- Judicially Managed Accountability and Recovery Court Act of 2021
NC.statewide_note: Optional per judicial district. AOC administered. Cases can be referred across counties.
NC.counties_note: 14 counties on nccourts.gov. Harnett was first NC VTC (2013). Rockingham opened May 2025.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: eligible -- NC more inclusive than federal standards
discharge_types.dishonorable: not verified -- statute silent; likely excluded per federal norms

eligibility.discharge_note: UNC School of Government: only requirement is prior military service. NC courts NOT limited to federal veteran definition.
eligibility.service_connection_detail: No formal service-connection requirement. Only prior military service required.
charge_exclusions: Varies by court -- no statewide statutory exclusions
Randolph County: Class H/I felony or lower (nonviolent)
General pattern: Class A-G felonies excluded
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: NC statute contains NO eligibility criteria. Entirely deferred to court discretion.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: No statewide policy. Prior convictions alone not automatic disqualifier.

program_details.completion_result: Charges reduced or dismissed via deferred prosecution or conditional discharge.

VA_STATE.statute: No standalone statute. Authority: Supreme Court of Virginia Rule 1:25 (Specialty Dockets). Va. Code 18.2-254.2 designates VTDs for federal grants.
VA_STATE.statewide_note: Optional per locality. 10 dockets as of March 2026 (4 Circuit, 5 GDC, 1 JDR).
VA_STATE.counties_note: 10 dockets across 8 localities. Directory updated March 27, 2026.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: varies -- half of dockets excluded non-honorable as of 2019; Fairfax appears inclusive

eligibility.service_connection_detail: Diagnosed mental health and/or substance use disorder required (DSM-5). Formal VA rating NOT required.
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: No statewide statutory exclusions. Many dockets incorrectly mirror drug court exclusions which do NOT apply to VTDs.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Varies. Many historically excluded prior violent felony within 10 years. Strategic plan recommended removing restriction.

program_details.completion_result: Non-violent felonies may be dismissed; charges reduced; alternatives to incarceration.

GA.statewide_note: Optional per county/circuit. Certified by Council of Accountability Court Judges (CACJ). State funding conditioned on certification.

discharge_types.other_than_honorable: varies -- Cobb and Atlantic accept all; Coweta requires honorable
discharge_types.dishonorable: varies -- Cobb and Atlantic explicitly accept; statute has no bar

eligibility.discharge_note: Statute defines veteran as former member of armed forces with NO discharge requirement.
eligibility.service_connection_detail: Statute does NOT require service connection. In practice, most courts target veterans with substance dependency and/or mental illness.
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: Statutory exclusions. Exception: reentry programs for incarcerated veterans may accept excluded charges.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Not addressed in statute. Courts set locally. Violent offense history generally disqualifies.

IL.statute: 730 ILCS 167/ (Veterans and Servicemembers Court Treatment Act)
IL.statewide_note: MANDATORY statewide since January 1, 2018 (P.A. 99-807). Each of 24 judicial circuits required to implement.
IL.counties_note: 23 counties verified. 11th Circuit is Illinois's only circuitwide problem-solving court.

discharge_types.bad_conduct: likely eligible -- technically distinct from dishonorable
discharge_types.dishonorable: excluded -- only discharge type barred by statute

eligibility.discharge_note: 730 ILCS 167/10: discharged under conditions other than dishonorable. Active servicemembers also eligible.
eligibility.service_connection_detail: No mandatory nexus requirement. Illinois does NOT require connection between charges and military conditions.
charge_exclusions: Predatory criminal sexual assault of a child
Offense involving discharge of a firearm
eligibility.charge_exclusions_note: Per 730 ILCS 167/20. Also excluded if crime of violence within past 5 years. Must be probation-eligible.
eligibility.prior_convictions_policy: Crime of violence within 5 years: excluded. Non-violent felonies: not automatic bar. Cook County: prior VTC within 3 years excluded.

program_details.completion_result: Dismissal or sentence termination. May vacate convictions for sealing/expungement.
conditions: Substance use treatment (MAT cannot be prohibited)
